issues.description: In class PersonResource, the GET-all endpoint mapping for the collection is inconsistent across artifacts. The template PersonResource defines getAllPersons() with @GetMapping("persons") (template: src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java), and the problem statement and tests expect endpoints under "/persons" (problem_statement.md references PUT /persons/... and tests use "/persons"). The solution's PersonResource instead defines the collection GET as @GetMapping("people") (solution: src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java). This naming mismatch ("persons" vs "people") can confuse students about the correct endpoint to call and creates an inconsistency between the solution implementation and the template/tests/assignment text.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection endpoint path consistent across all artifacts. Prefer changing the solution's @GetMapping("people") to @GetMapping("persons") so the solution, template, tests, and problem statement consistently use "/persons" (or, alternatively, update template/tests/problem text to use "/people" if you prefer that naming).

issues.description: Concept: HTTP GET endpoint that returns all Person resources. Problem statement and automated tests refer to the collection endpoint as '/persons' (e.g., integration test steps and endpoint usage in the problem text and tests). Template PersonResource declares the GET mapping as @GetMapping("persons"). The solution PersonResource declares the GET mapping as @GetMapping("people"). This naming divergence ("persons" vs "people") refers to the same conceptual endpoint but uses different path identifiers across artifacts. A student reading the problem and using the template will expect and test against '/persons', but the solution implementation exposes '/people', causing confusion and potentially failing endpoint-based integration tests or manual verification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the collection GET endpoint name across all artifacts. Preferred quick fix: change the solution's PersonResource @GetMapping("people") to @GetMapping("persons") so the exposed endpoint matches the problem statement and tests ('/persons'). Alternatively, if you prefer 'people', update the problem statement, template tests, and all references to use '/people' consistently. Ensure tests and documentation use the same path as the implemented mapping.
